subject: docs/coop/artifacts/platform-tcb-contract.v4.json

blockers.title: The range and filesystem escape forms still do not define a closed, reproducible platform selector language
evidence: EXACT-BUILD accepts either a platform-published build or version string but carries no identifier-kind, publisher/variant namespace, or comparison-scheme identifier. CLOSED-RANGE then says its endpoints use that same type, so it does not require both endpoints to be build identifiers under one scheme or version identifiers under one scheme.

CLOSED-RANGE delegates ordering to 'the platform-published total order on the canonical identifier' without naming an order, algorithm, source, or version. A generic osFamily=linux profile identifies no distribution/publisher that could supply one total order, and the contract forbids the population packet from minting missing range semantics.

The filesystem escape other:<digest-bound-fstype-token> defines no tagged structure, digest algorithm identifier, encoding, length, or validation rule. An arbitrary other:anything string can therefore occupy the supposedly canonical identifier form under one conforming reader.
blockers.impact: The same range endpoints or filesystem escape can compare differently across verifiers, and Linux version strings from different publishers can collide or be incomparable under one profile key. A frozen allowlist and its G22 matrix therefore remain non-deterministic even though all required members are present.
blockers.requiredRepair: Give version/build selectors an explicit identifierScheme/publisher-or-variant discriminator and a versioned comparison algorithm; require both range endpoints to share that scheme and define membership entirely in this contract, or prohibit CLOSED-RANGE until such a scheme exists. Define the filesystem escape as a structured tag with an approved algorithm identifier and exact digest encoding/length, or remove it.

shouldFix.title: SONAME-ABI is described as an optional companion but no conforming signed entry can encode it
shouldFix.evidence: Every signed entry must carry exactly one identityEvidence tag from classMap. SONAME-ABI appears in no classMap list, while comparison says it may accompany libc authenticity evidence; signedEntry has no compatibilitySelectors field and no authenticity-tag payload defines a SONAME-ABI subfield.
shouldFix.impact: One producer must drop the purported compatibility selector, another must smuggle a second tag into the exactly-one identity union, and a third can extend the exhaustive four-field entry. The authenticity repair itself holds, but the emitted schema is not deterministic.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Either remove SONAME-ABI and its companion-language entirely, or define it as a closed optional subfield inside the permitted libc authenticity-evidence payload with explicit non-identity comparison semantics. Do not reintroduce it as sole authenticity evidence or an unrostered fifth signed-entry field.

verdictBasis: REJECT: 1 blocker and 1 SHOULD-FIX. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
conclusion: REJECT. The platform selector language remains non-reproducible across conforming verifiers, and the SONAME-ABI companion remains unencodable in the exhaustive signed-entry schema. DR-126 remains OPEN; no D-096 (A) grant, qualification, satisfaction, sealing, application, or implementation authority is created.
